newsitem.title: USA: Barge traffic continues to be slow on Illinois.
newsitem.headline: Barge traffic continues to be slow on Illinois.

text.p: High water on the upper end of the Illinois River was beginning to subside but barge traffic was slow, a U.S. Army Corp of Engineers official said.

"Water is still high from Ottawa, Ill., to the mouth of the Illinois River, near Grafton," said Rick Granados, chief of Lock and Dam Section for the Illinois Waterway Project, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.

"But we think the Illinois River will crest at Peoria today (Tuesday)," he said. As of 0800 CST, the Illinois River at Peoria was at 24.6 feet versus 23.5 feet at 0800 on Monday. Flood stage at Peoria is 18 feet, the Corps said.

U.S. cost, insurance and freight (CIF) soybean and corn values rose on Monday and Tuesday in the nearby positions, underpinned by possible problems loading barges on sections of the Illinois River, export sources said.
A cash merchandiser in Hennepin, Ill., said his was one of the few facilities in the area that was able to load barges in the high water.
He said he expects the river to drop three to four feet in the next two days.
Rising water fed by heavy rains late last week forced the closure of several locks on the Illinois River this week.
Granados noted Starved Rock Lock near Utica, Ill., remained closed. However, he said he anticipated the lock to be up by late Tuesday.
Marseilles Lock at Marseilles, Ill., and Dresden Island Lock, near Morris, Ill., reopened on Monday but with "configuration restrictions," he said.
At Beardstown, Ill., the high water had not yet crested and the forecast this week was for more rain in that area, Granados said.
"If those weather conditions come out as predicted, yes, we could expect more flooding problems," Granados added.
